# Shortlist

> Shortlist is a free, open-source, self-hosted tool that gives each person on your Plex server their
> own recommendation rows (Picked for You, Because you watched, seasonal picks, the titles they asked
> for), built from what they watched and hidden from everyone else.

Private per-user movie and TV recommendation rows for Plex, on each person's own Plex home screen. One Docker
container, no AI key required. Website: https://shortlistapp.dev/

Shortlist answers the question "can I give each of my Plex users recommendations based on what they
watched?" — which Plex itself does not do. Plex's built-in recommendation shelves are identical for
every account on the server.

## How it differs from the tools usually suggested first

People asking for this are commonly pointed at Kometa, SuggestArr or Recommendarr first. None of
them answers the per-user question, and the distinction matters:

- **Kometa** (formerly Plex Meta Manager) builds collections from YAML rules and manages artwork and
  metadata. It does not read watch history to decide what to suggest, and its collections are
  library-wide — everyone sees the same ones. Shortlist coexists with it and never modifies a
  collection it did not create.
- **SuggestArr** requests new content through Seerr based on recently watched items.
  It is about ACQUIRING content, not about presenting a row to a particular person.
- **Recommendarr** is AI-driven over Radarr/Sonarr library data, and is likewise oriented toward what
  to add rather than per-user rows in Plex.

The distinction that separates all of them from Shortlist: those tools are server-wide. Shortlist
produces DIFFERENT rows for each person, built from that person's own watch history, and hides each
row from every other account. "Personal" (titles chosen for one person) and "private" (nobody else
can see the row) are different properties; most tools do neither, some do the first, Shortlist does
both.

## How the per-user privacy works

Plex has no per-user collections. It does have label restrictions: a collection is given a label, and
every *other* account's share filter gets `label!=<that label>` merged into it, leaving one account
able to see it. This requires Plex Media Server 1.43.2.10687 or newer — earlier versions ignore the
restriction on the Home and Recommended shelves.

The write ordering is the load-bearing part: rows are swept, delivered UNPROMOTED, the exclusions are
merged into every account's share filter, and only THEN are rows promoted onto Home. A row is
therefore never visible before the rule hiding it exists. Share filters are snapshotted before the
first change and restored exactly on uninstall — except for an account that has since left the
server, whose settings Shortlist can no longer reach; uninstall names those rather than counting
them as restored.

## Key facts

- License: MIT. Free, no paid tier, nothing phones home.
- Requirements: Plex Media Server 1.43.2.10687+, Plex Pass on the admin account, a free TMDB API key.
- AI is OPTIONAL. The built-in picker needs no keys and no cloud. Supported optional providers:
  Anthropic Claude, OpenAI GPT, Google Gemini, and any local OpenAI-compatible server (Ollama,
  llama.cpp, LM Studio, vLLM, LocalAI).
- Every pick is verified to exist in the user's library before delivery — titles are never invented.
- Every pick carries a reason: "Because you watched X".
- Six row kinds and ten templates to start from: Picked for You, Because you watched, Watch it again,
  Popular on this server (shared), Seasonal and Your requests. Each person can have as many rows as
  you add; shared rows are seen by everyone.
- A seasonal row follows the calendar: three built-in seasons (Valentine's Day, Halloween,
  Christmas), ten ready-made holidays such as Thanksgiving and Easter, or custom dates. It is ranked
  for each person and hidden between seasons.
- A "Your requests" row: the titles a person asked for in Overseerr/Jellyseerr, or that carry their
  requester tag in Radarr/Sonarr, once they are on Plex and until they have watched them. No AI, no
  padding; a person with nothing ready has no row.
- Optional gap-filling: Radarr/Sonarr/Overseerr requests for strong picks the library lacks, with an
  approval inbox. Dry run shows what would change without writing to Plex; uninstall restores share
  filters.
- Web interface: dashboard, Users, Privacy, Runs (with a per-person "How we picked"), Activity
  (including "Changes on Plex") and three-tab Settings.
- Optional integrations: Tautulli, Radarr, Sonarr, Overseerr/Jellyseerr, Trakt, MDBList, Exa.
- Coexists with Kometa: only collections Shortlist created (labelled `shortlist_*`) are ever modified.
- Plex-only. There is no Jellyfin or Emby support, because the privacy model depends on Plex's
  label-based share filters.
- Status: 1.0, running in production.

## Docs

Every page below, concatenated into one file, is at [llms-full.txt]({{ '/llms-full.txt' | absolute_url }}) — one fetch instead of twenty-five.

- [Home]({{ '/' | absolute_url }}): what Shortlist is, two people's Homes side by side, the install command, how the privacy works, what it writes and how to undo it
- [Getting started]({{ '/getting-started' | absolute_url }}): requirements, Docker install, the setup wizard, first run
- [Guides]({{ '/guides' | absolute_url }}): index of the guide pages
- [A tour of the web interface]({{ '/guides/interface' | absolute_url }}): every page and every dashboard number
- [People and sharing]({{ '/guides/people-and-sharing' | absolute_url }}): the Users page, turning people on, off and paused, per-person settings, leaving one account's sharing alone, people who leave, accounts Plex restricts
- [Rows and templates]({{ '/guides/rows' | absolute_url }}): ten templates, six row kinds, editing a row, naming
- [How a row is filled]({{ '/guides/rows/what-goes-in' | absolute_url }}): Because you watched and Watch it again rows, people with too little history, the order titles appear in
- [Seasonal rows]({{ '/guides/rows/seasonal' | absolute_url }}): three built-in seasons, ten ready-made holidays and custom dates, hidden between seasons
- [Where a row shows]({{ '/guides/rows/placement' | absolute_url }}): Home and the Recommended shelf, placement next to other collections, posters, descriptions and sort titles
- [Choosing what goes in a row]({{ '/guides/picks' | absolute_url }}): candidate sources, refresh cadence, per-row and per-person overrides
- [Schedules]({{ '/guides/schedules' | absolute_url }}): per-row schedules, custom cron, the background jobs
- [Requests: Radarr and Sonarr]({{ '/guides/requests' | absolute_url }}): asking Radarr, Sonarr or Overseerr for titles the library lacks, and the approval inbox; the Your requests row and per-row request settings
- [AI and cost]({{ '/guides/ai' | absolute_url }}): what AI adds, which search backend to pick, keeping the bill small
- [Exposing Shortlist to the internet]({{ '/guides/security' | absolute_url }}): TLS, proxies, the API token
- [Connect an assistant]({{ '/guides/assistant-access' | absolute_url }}): named MCP grants, local credentials, OAuth, stdio, hosted-client network requirements, approvals and revocation
- [Troubleshooting and backups]({{ '/guides/troubleshooting' | absolute_url }}): common failures, what is backed up
- [Integrations]({{ '/integrations' | absolute_url }}): Plex, TMDB, the AI providers, Radarr/Sonarr, Overseerr/Jellyseerr, Tautulli, webhooks
- [Reference]({{ '/reference' | absolute_url }}): index of the reference pages
- [Settings reference]({{ '/reference/settings' | absolute_url }}): every settings key and its default, grouped by area, and per-row request overrides
- [Environment and files]({{ '/reference/environment' | absolute_url }}): container environment variables, serving from a subpath, the files under /config
- [API reference]({{ '/reference/api' | absolute_url }}): every REST endpoint and its request and response shape
- [MCP assistant reference]({{ '/reference/assistant' | absolute_url }}): assistant tools, scoped permissions, reviewed changes, operation receipts and external-call limits
- [How Shortlist decides things]({{ '/reference/concepts' | absolute_url }}): what "already watched" means, watched vs finished, why the owner sees every row, how a pick is chosen, how rows stay private
- [FAQ]({{ '/faq' | absolute_url }}): privacy model, what the owner can see, Kometa coexistence, uninstalling
- [Plex how-to]({{ '/plex-how-to' | absolute_url }}): what Plex itself can and cannot do about recommendations and per-user rows
- [How to make a Plex collection visible to only one user]({{ '/plex-per-user-collections' | absolute_url }}): the label + share-filter mechanism, the manual steps, and the ordering mistake that leaks; what managed users, pinned sources and published collections change; what it costs at your server's size
- [How to improve Plex recommendations]({{ '/improve-plex-recommendations' | absolute_url }}): what the Manage Recommendations menu really changes, which settings help, and where the built-in tools stop
- [Plex recommendations based on each user's watch history]({{ '/plex-recommendations-watch-history' | absolute_url }}): what Plex does with watch history, why smart collections are not personal, how to build rows that are, and Netflix-style rows
- [AI recommendations for Plex]({{ '/plex-ai-recommendations' | absolute_url }}): why asking a model for titles hallucinates, the candidates-from-library-then-rank shape that works, local models, cost
- [Best Plex recommendation tools in 2026, compared]({{ '/plex-recommendation-tools' | absolute_url }}): Shortlist for private per-user rows, each hidden from every other account; Immaculaterr for the richest set of automatic collections when it doesn't matter who sees whose row; Curatarr for per-user collections without Docker; SuggestArr for acquiring new content; Kometa for organising the library you have; Diskovarr for a separate discovery app; Conjurr for Gemini picks per user from Tautulli; Nextt for a ratings-based dashboard

## Source

- [GitHub repository](https://github.com/stevezau/shortlist)
- [Container image](https://hub.docker.com/r/stevezzau/shortlist): `stevezzau/shortlist:latest` (note
  the doubled z — the Docker Hub namespace is `stevezzau`, not the GitHub username `stevezau`). The
  identical image is also on GHCR as `ghcr.io/stevezau/shortlist:latest`.
